name: Little Later
tagline: Local-first Chrome extension for visual bookmarks, tasks, reminders, notes, and AI assist.
description: Little Later is a Manifest V3 Chrome extension with no backend. The 500 by 600 popup keeps visual bookmarks, tasks, reminders, and notes in one Dexie IndexedDB database, with every record encrypted under its profile's key. The service worker is the only writer: it captures tabs, fires reminder notifications, runs context-menu actions, and applies typed commands sent by the popup and the AI. AI Assist talks to Ollama, LM Studio, or a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint and will not write or export until the user confirms in chat.
highlights: Shipped as a self-contained MV3 extension: React popup plus a service worker for tab capture, alarms, notifications, and context menus.
Each record is sealed with AES-256-GCM under a per-profile key; a password wraps that key with PBKDF2-SHA-256 at 600,000 iterations, and locking drops the unwrapped key.
The service worker is the only writer: the popup and the AI send typed commands, which run one at a time.
Times are epoch milliseconds and recurrence is an anchored rule computed with Temporal, so recurring times follow the device across time zones.
AI Assist uses the OpenAI SDK against Ollama, LM Studio, or a custom compatible URL. Reads run immediately; writes and exports wait for in-chat Confirm.

CI runs format, lint, typecheck, unit, property-based and Playwright end-to-end tests, CodeQL, OpenSSF Scorecard and workflow audits. Tagged releases ship a zip, a signed CRX, a CycloneDX SBOM, checksums and signed build provenance.

Public GitHub Releases exist for v1.0.0, v2.0.0 (extension-only rebuild), v2.1.0 (confirmed writes), v2.1.1 (security fixes and supply-chain hardening), v3.0.0 (encrypted storage format v1) and v3.0.1.

story.why: Keep browsing captures, tasks, reminders, and notes in the browser profile instead of a hosted account, and let a local model act on that data only after a click.
story.problem: Bookmarks, todos, reminders, and notes usually live in separate cloud products. A local-only Chrome popup needs capture, encryption, notifications, and optional AI without a server.
challenges: The MV3 service worker suspends, so alarms drive reminders and catch up on missed fires. (src/background/scheduler.ts)
The whole product UI is a 500 by 600 HashRouter popup, not a website. (src/popup/index.css)
Local Ollama and LM Studio reject the extension Origin, so a DNR rule rewrites it for the extension's own requests only. (src/background/localAIOriginRule.ts)
Reminders must fire while a profile is locked, so schedules stay readable while their text stays encrypted. (src/storage/schema.ts)
Backups are a chunked, encrypted .lldat format that imports into a new profile with fresh keys. (src/storage/backup.ts)
Unsaved history is capped per site and overall so capture cannot grow without bound. (src/background/commands/saves.ts)
designDecisions: Stay a Chrome extension with no backend or hosted sync. (manifest.json)
Encrypt each record under a wrapped profile key, in one versioned database. (src/storage/schema.ts)
Make the service worker the only writer, through typed commands. (src/background/commands/)
Store instants as epoch milliseconds and recurrence as anchored rules. (packages/shared/src/utils/schedule.ts)
Queue mutate, destructive, and export AI tools until in-chat Confirm. (src/services/ai/main.ts)
Use built-in local URLs for Ollama and LM Studio; Custom supplies its own. (src/services/ai/config.ts)

future.next: Build the AI tools on the worker commands with defineTool, and decide the product direction for AI features.
roadmap: A design-system pass across the popup, fixing the React Compiler lint warnings screen by screen.
The Playwright visual tour is still a local script, not a CI job.
upcomingFeatures: Note the current webpage from AI Assist
Link a note to the current webpage from AI Assist
ideas: More than one profile unlocked at once.
